task.description: Root-cause ISS-0397: Letflow.Engine.build_instance_state/3 (lib/letflow/engine.ex ~line 1813) hardcodes join_counters: %{} on every complete_task/3 call, so a PARALLEL_GATEWAY join can only fire within the same hop-chain as its own split. Diagnosis only -- route to CODE-DESIGNER for a fix design.

result.summary:
1) EXACT MECHANISM -- confirmed by reading code directly, not by trusting the issue's prose or the RELEASE-VALIDATOR's recommendation_to_orch verbatim. Letflow.Engine.build_snapshot_and_state/4 (engine.ex ~1721) is complete_task/3's per-call state-reconstruction path. It builds InstanceState.t() from three LIVE tables read fresh every call: fetch_graph/2 (immutable process_definitions snapshot via Letflow.Definitions.SnapshotStore -- a DIFFERENT 'snapshot' table, definition-graph only), load_active_tokens/3 (tokens), and load_pending_task_tokens/3 (tasks). It never calls Letflow.Engine.SnapshotWriter.latest_snapshot/2 anywhere -- SnapshotWriter (REQ-054) is not wired into this read path at all. build_instance_state/3 (~1813) then hardcodes join_counters: %{} with a code comment stating plainly: 'no table persists JoinCounter state across calls today.' That comment is accurate: no `tokens`, `tasks`, or `instance_projections` column stores JoinCounter.t() state, and the one table that DOES serialize join_counters (instance_state_snapshots, REQ-054/SnapshotWriter.take_snapshot/4, confirmed by reading serialize_state/1 at snapshot_writer.ex:233-241 which explicitly includes 'join_counters') is never read by build_snapshot_and_state/4. So this is a real, confirmed omission, not a misdiagnosis -- but it is NOT simply 'a field that's already being written correctly just needs to be read back,' which is why point 3 below matters.

2) WHY RELEASE-VALIDATOR'S ONE-LINE HYPOTHESIS IS INCOMPLETE (important for CODE-DESIGNER). SnapshotWriter's persistence is PERIODIC, not per-call: snapshot_instance/4 (engine.ex:1135) calls SnapshotWriter.maybe_take_snapshot/4, which only inserts a new instance_state_snapshots row when current_sequence_number - last_snapshot_sequence_number >= interval (default 1000 events -- snapshot_writer.ex:117,167-198). Confirmed via req054-instance-state-snapshots.md INV-ISS-2 and the design doc's own §6 discussion: this table is a REQ-053-style crash-recovery/replay artifact (see INV-ISS-1, 'reconstruct_instance/2's result via {:from_snapshot,...} and via {:full_replay,1} are equal'), not intended or built as a live per-call state cache. Consequence: if a naive fix simply wired build_snapshot_and_state/4 to call SnapshotWriter.latest_snapshot/2 and copy its join_counters into build_instance_state/3, the result would be JOIN_COUNTERS AS OF UP TO 999 EVENTS AGO on most calls, not the instance's live join_counters -- silently WRONG (stale expected_from_branches/received_from_branches/cancelled_branches), which is worse than today's typed {:error, {:unknown_branch_id, _}} failure (today's gap fails loud, per REQ-048 design doc's own INV-EE48-7 -- 'never silently mismerges'). A correct fix therefore needs join_counters made durable and CURRENT as of every complete_task/3 call that mutates it (split-creation, one-branch-arrival, cancel-branch, or full-join-fire), not merely 'read the field already being written' -- this is a genuinely deeper design problem than a missing read, even though the writing mechanism (SnapshotWriter) already exists for an unrelated purpose.

3) DELIBERATE-EXCLUSION CHECK -- confirmed NOT deliberately excluded, but also confirmed NOT closed by REQ-054 despite REQ-048 naming REQ-054 as the closer. REQ-048 design doc (req048-instance-completion-engine-shell.md) §11/§13, INV-EE48-7 and OQ-3 (MAJOR) state explicitly: 'join_counters: %{} always... a hop-chain reaching a :PARALLEL_GATEWAY join fails with a typed error, never silently mismerges... explicitly deferred to whichever requirement first persists join-counter state across complete_task calls' and its own cross-reference table lists 'REQ-054 (snapshot/join-counter persistence, not yet built) | Future | is exactly what REQ-054 would close.' Read req054-instance-state-snapshots.md in full: it never revisits or declines that expectation -- it simply implements a periodic snapshot/replay mechanism (REQ-053's sibling) that happens to serialize join_counters as one of InstanceState.t()'s five fields (moduledoc: '`take_snapshot/4` serialises exactly InstanceState.t()'s own fields: status, tokens, variables, pending_task_nodes, and join_counters'), without ever wiring itself into complete_task/3's hot-path reconstruction or addressing OQ-3 by name anywhere in its own text. This is an honest scope gap between two requirements' authors' expectations, not a recorded decision to leave OQ-3 open -- ISS-0397's own description ('never actually closed by REQ-054') is accurate.

4) RELATIONSHIP TO ISS-0396 -- CONFIRMED DISTINCT, no overlap, fixing one will not resolve or interact with the other. Read docs/issues/ISS-0396.yaml in full: it is an Ecto.Multi :task_records key-collision defect in build_complete_task_tail_multi/6's SUB_PROCESS-child-completion-cascade branch (engine.ex ~2381-2494), triggered when 2+ SUB_PROCESS children spawned from the same hop chain both complete synchronously in the same parent transaction. ISS-0397 touches a completely different function (build_instance_state/3, the M3 state-SEED step at the top of run_complete_task/6, ~1728/1813) and a completely different data structure (join_counters map vs. the task_records Multi step's changeset list). Both live in engine.ex and both surface via complete_task/3, but neither reads nor writes the other's state, and fixing ISS-0397 (join_counters durability) has no bearing on the task_records Ecto.Multi key-collision mechanism, and vice versa. Safe to fix independently, in either order.

5) RELATIONSHIP TO ISS-0398 -- CONFIRMED DISTINCT (already known qualitatively from the issue tags, but verified by reading the actual diff). ISS-0398 (PR #783, merged) fixed Letflow.Engine.Transition's walk_to_gateway/collect_leaf_gateways graph-traversal analysis (finding the matching join node across a fork branch containing a multi-outgoing-edge node like an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY) via Tarjan-SCC memoization -- a pure, in-memory, single-call graph-shape problem, with 2 real BLOCKER reworks (exponential blowup, then memo-key unsoundness under legal cycles-through-gateways). ISS-0397 is a cross-call PERSISTENCE problem (join_counters not surviving between separate complete_task/3 invocations) -- neither the code path (Transition graph analysis vs. Engine.build_instance_state/3 DB reconstruction) nor the failure mode (structural graph-walk defect vs. missing durable state) overlaps.

6) EXISTING TEST COVERAGE -- CONFIRMED ZERO coverage of the actual defect path. test/letflow/engine/parallel_gateway_test.exs (12 tests, including all of ISS-0398's additions) is declared 'Pure module, no Letflow.Repo/Ecto.Sandbox dependency anywhere in this file' (its own moduledoc) -- every test constructs an InstanceState.t() directly in memory and calls Letflow.Engine.Transition functions synchronously in a single process/call; none goes through Letflow.Engine.complete_task/3, none touches the tasks/tokens/instance_projections tables, and therefore none can exercise (or would have caught) a cross-DB-call join_counters loss. The only place this defect is actually exercised end-to-end is test/letflow/simulation/req208_meridian_test.exs's two loan-origination scenarios, which assert the CURRENT BROKEN behavior (a real HTTP 500 on the second, separate complete_task call) as their closed disposition -- i.e. they document the bug, they do not test correct cross-call join behavior, and per RELEASE-VALIDATOR's own REQ-208 sign-off those two ACs are recorded PARTIALLY MET specifically because of this gap. A correct fix will need new test coverage that drives a real PARALLEL_GATEWAY split via Letflow.Engine.create/2, completes each branch's HUMAN_TASK via SEPARATE complete_task/3 calls (not a single in-memory Transition.transition/3 sequence), and asserts the join fires correctly on the final branch's completion -- this does not exist anywhere in the current test suite today.

7) COMPLEXITY/RIGOR FLAG FOR CODE-DESIGNER AND ORCH -- this is NOT a simple 'add the missing read' fix, and warrants ISS-0398-level rigor for two independent reasons: (a) per point 2, naively reading back a stale periodic snapshot would introduce a SILENT correctness regression (stale join_counters) where today's failure is at least loud/typed -- any design must guarantee the join_counters read on a given complete_task/3 call reflects every join_counters mutation from every complete_task/3 call that has committed before it, which is a live-consistency property, not a replay-cadence one; (b) REQ-199's correlated-effect-ordering work (named explicitly in the task brief) is relevant because join_counters mutations (branch arrival, cancel-branch, fire-join) must be linearized correctly against concurrent complete_task/3 calls on sibling branches of the SAME split -- the existing M1/M2 row-lock ordering (fetch_and_lock_task before fetch_and_lock_instance_projection, per engine.ex's own documented lock-ordering rule at ~line 257) is what currently serializes concurrent branch completions; a join_counters persistence design must either piggyback on that same lock (e.g. store join_counters on the already-locked instance_projections row or a row it directly joins against) or introduce its own compatible locking discipline -- inventing a second, differently-scoped lock for join_counters risk a genuine lock-ordering deadlock class this codebase has been careful to avoid elsewhere. CODE-DESIGNER should treat this as a correctness-sensitive design requiring explicit invariant statements (an INV- entry analogous to INV-EE48-7) and TEST-DESIGNER should plan concurrent-branch-completion test coverage, not just a single serial two-call happy path.

8) CONCRETE FIX DIRECTION (for CODE-DESIGNER to evaluate, not a prescribed implementation): the most direct option is a new durable, always-current store for join_counters keyed by instance_id -- either (a) a new column on instance_projections (already row-locked by M2 on every complete_task/3 call, giving lock-ordering compatibility for free) holding the serialized join_counters map, updated transactionally in the same Multi step(s) that currently mutate instance_state.join_counters in-memory (Transition's dispatch_parallel_split/4, dispatch_parallel_join/4, dispatch_cancel_branch/3 -- engine/transition.ex lines ~777-796, ~1043-1057, ~1095-1182), and read back into build_instance_state/3 in place of the hardcoded %{}; or (b) a new dedicated join_counters table row-locked alongside instance_projections in M2. Both close the gap; (a) is simpler and reuses existing lock ordering, (b) keeps instance_projections' schema unchanged but needs its own lock-compatibility argument. CODE-DESIGNER should also decide the serialize/deserialize shape (SnapshotWriter's existing join_counter_entry_to_map/from_map at snapshot_writer.ex:252-306 is a ready-made, already-reviewed serialization format that could be reused rather than re-invented, even though the target table differs from instance_state_snapshots).
result.recommendation_to_orch: Route to Step 2 CODE-DESIGNER: design a durable, always-current (not periodic-snapshot-based) persistence mechanism for InstanceState.join_counters keyed by instance_id, written transactionally wherever Transition mutates join_counters (split/branch-arrival/cancel/fire, engine/transition.ex ~777-1182) under the same lock ordering complete_task/3's M1/M2 already establish, and read back into Letflow.Engine.build_instance_state/3 (engine.ex ~1813) in place of the hardcoded join_counters: %{}. Do not resolve this by wiring in Letflow.Engine.SnapshotWriter/REQ-054's periodic (every-1000-event) snapshot table as the read source -- that would silently reintroduce stale join_counters reads, a correctness regression worse than today's loud typed failure. Flag for TEST-DESIGNER: no existing test drives a real cross-call (separate complete_task/3 invocations, real Repo/Ecto.Sandbox) PARALLEL_GATEWAY join today -- new coverage is required, including a concurrent-sibling-branch-completion scenario, not just a serial two-call happy path. Confirmed distinct from and non-interacting with ISS-0396 (Ecto.Multi :task_records collision, different function/data structure) and ISS-0398 (Transition graph-traversal fix, already merged, different code path) -- no shared root cause, safe to fix independently. Given the staleness/locking subtlety in point 7 of the summary, this should get the same rigor (explicit invariant statement, CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR scrutiny of the locking argument, concurrent-completion test coverage) that ISS-0398 needed after its 2 BLOCKER reworks, not a fast-tracked single-pass fix.
